title: 1979–80 National Hurling League

{{Short description|49th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1979–80 National Hurling League |image = |dates =4 November 1979 – 26 October 1980 |teams = |team1 = Cork |captain1 = [[Dermot Mac Curtain]] |manager1 = [[Len Gaynor]] |titles = 11th |team2 = Limerick |captain2 =[[Seán Foley]] |manager2 = [[Noel Drumgoole]] |two= Wicklow |three = Mayo |previous = [[1978–79 National Hurling League|1978–79]] |next = [[1980–81 National Hurling League|1980–81]] }} The '''1979–80 National Hurling League''' was the 49th season of the [[National Hurling League]] (NHL), an annual [[hurling]] competition for the [[GAA county teams]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}}{{cite book |last= Smith|first=Raymond |date=1999 |title=Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games |location=Dublin, Ireland |page=208 |isbn=0950175870}} It was won by {{GG|Cork|hurling}}. ==Overview== ===Structure=== The National Hurling League's top division was divided into two groups - 1A and 1B. The top two teams in Division 1A advance to the semi-finals. The third- and fourth-placed teams in 1A, as well as the top two from 1B, play in the quarter-finals. The bottom two teams in 1A are relegated, while the top two teams in 1B are promoted. The bottom team in 1B is relegated, while the Division 2 champions are promoted. ==Overview== ===Division 1=== The National Hurling League's top division featured fourteen teams divided into two equal groups - 1A and 1B. Each group consisted of seven teams. The top two teams from Division 1A automatically qualified for the knock-out semi-finals. The third and fourth placed teams, as well as the top two teams from Division 1B, contested two lone quarter-finals. In spite of losing two group games and finishing second in Division 1A, [[Cork GAA|Cork]] won the league title following a 4-15 to 4-6 defeat of [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in a replay of the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} Down at the other end of the tables, [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Clare GAA|Clare]] won just two of their group stage games and were both relegated to Division 1B. They swapped places with [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] and [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] who finished in first and second positions respectively in Division 1B. [[Kildare GAA|Kildare]] finished the group stage without a single win and were relegated to Division 2. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1979-80 |winners=[[Cork GAA|Cork]]
